amendments.rule: Rule 55's correlative clause is not peculiar to a crasis. Where a **separate** `καί` answers a preceding comparative `καθώς` or `ὡς`, that `καί` takes the whole English correlative — *so* or *even so* — and the comparative adverb keeps only *as* or *even as*. `καθὼς … καὶ ὑμεῖς` → *as … so ye* gives *so* to the conjunction at JHN.6.57 and JHN.13.33, as `ὡς … καὶ` → *As … so* does at GAL.1.9 and 2CO.13.2, and as `καθὼς ἐκεῖνός ἐστιν καὶ ἡμεῖς ἐσμεν` → *as he is, even so are we* does at 1JN.4.17. Rule 55 already gives the reason and it does not depend on the crasis: the comparative adverb has its own English word already, and the correlative is what the `καί` writes. The corpus confirms it from the other side, `καθώς` being rendered *even as*, *as* or *according as* in all sixty-nine of its units and never taking *so*. Rule 17 heads such a unit on ***so***, the word that realizes the correlative; a supplied *even* is an intensifying helper on it under rules 7 and 11, exactly as it is where `οὕτως` takes *even so* at JHN.3.14, JHN.5.21, JHN.5.26 and JHN.14.31 and where `ναί` does at REV.1.7. So do not head such a unit on *even* merely because *even* is the more direct gloss of `καί`: that gloss is what a bare *even* answers to where no *so* competes, as at 2CO.11.12 and EPH.2.3, and it does not carry where the ASV writes the correlative out. Where the ASV writes **no** correlative and renders the comparative together with its answering `καί` by a bare *even as*, that is exactly where the gloss does carry: the `καί` is `aligned` to *even* and headed on it, and the comparative keeps a bare *as* as its own unit, as `καθὼς καὶ ἡμεῖς` → *even as we* does at 2CO.11.12 and `ὡς καὶ οἱ λοιποί` → *even as the rest* at EPH.2.3. Do not give *even as* whole to the comparative and leave the `καί` `unrepresented`: rule 65's English-side test empties an intensifying `καί` only where the ASV writes no word for it, and a written *even* is such a word. A comparative with **no** answering `καί` is the contrast and keeps *even as* whole under rules 7 and 11, no other source token standing to claim the supplied *even*, so a chapter writing both — `καθώς` alone as *even as* and `καθὼς καί` as *even* plus *as* — is following rule 24's habit and not two analyses. The test is whether a `καί` stands in the construction, and never how the same comparative was rendered where none did.
amendments.why: This chapter's 2:14 (καθὼς καὶ αὐτοί -> 'even as they did') gave 'even as' whole to καθώς and emptied the καί, reading the rule's heading clause as though it settled placement. It does not: the clause about a bare 'even' is a parenthetical inside a sentence about heading a unit that contains 'so', and it names 2CO.11.12 and EPH.2.3 only in passing. 2CO.11.12 is καθὼς καὶ ἡμεῖς -> 'even as we', the identical construction to 1TH.2.14, and EPH.2.3 is ὡς καὶ οἱ λοιποί -> 'even as the rest'; both are corpus units in which the bare 'even' answers to the particle. The amendment states that placement in terms, names the two cited units as its examples, and marks off the contrast (a comparative with no answering καί, as at 1TH.2.4) so the widened rule cannot be read back onto it. It adds no new analysis and contradicts nothing in the corpus: it makes explicit what rule 82 already asserted and what rule 65's English-side test independently requires. Returned as an amendment rather than a new rule because the over-broad reading lives in rule 82's own closing sentence, and a cross-reference would leave that sentence in place for whoever reads it first.

conventions: Versification. The projection and the ASV divide this chapter differently at two places, and both are handled under rule 37 with each side recorded. The ASV renders δυνάμενοι ἐν βάρει εἶναι ὡς Χριστοῦ ἀπόστολοι (1TH.2.7 s001-s007) at the end of its verse 6, so those seven tokens are unrepresented in 2:7 and the English 'when we might have claimed authority as apostles of Christ' is added in 2:6. The ASV renders παρακαλοῦντες ὑμᾶς καὶ παραμυθούμενοι καὶ μαρτυρόμενοι (1TH.2.12 s001-s006) at the end of its verse 11, so those six tokens are unrepresented in 2:12 and 'exhorting you and encouraging you and testifying' is added in 2:11. Neither verse reaches across, and a reference comparison reports all thirteen source tokens as disagreements without that being a correction.

καθώς and an answering καί. Where the ASV writes a bare 'even as' with no correlative 'so', the 'even' is the καί's and the comparative keeps a bare 'as' (2:14, καθὼς καὶ αὐτοί -> 'even as they did'). Where no καί stands, nothing else can claim the supplied 'even' and the comparative keeps 'even as' whole (2:4). The chapter's other comparatives are bare 'as' (2:2, 2:5, 2:13, and καθάπερ at 2:11).

Possessive expressions. A reflexive ἑαυτοῦ or the adjective ἴδιος rendered by a two-word English possessive takes that whole expression as one unit headed on 'own', never on the pronominal word: 'her own' (2:7), 'our own' (2:8), 'his own' (2:11, 2:12), 'your own' (2:14). The pronominal is the possessor form English syntax requires, and 'own' is what realizes the reflexive or the ἴδιος sense; the governing article is displaced under rules 20 and 47 in every one of these five units.

report: One genuine error, at 1TH.2.14. καθὼς καὶ αὐτοί -> 'even as they did' gave 'even as' whole to καθώς (s028) and left the answering καί (s029) unrepresented. Rule 82's closing sentence names 2CO.11.12 (καθὼς καὶ ἡμεῖς -> 'even as we', the identical construction) and EPH.2.3 (ὡς καὶ οἱ λοιποί -> 'even as the rest') as the units where the bare-'even' gloss carries to the καί. Patched: καί -> 'even' headed on 'even', καθώς -> a bare 'as'. Rule 65's English-side test empties an intensifying καί only where the ASV writes no word for it, and here it wrote one.

This is not a split against 2:4, where καθώς stands with no answering καί and rightly keeps 'even as' whole, the supplied 'even' having no other source token to claim it. The difference is licensed by the source, and the convention log now records it.

Cross-verse checks that cleared. The 48 ὁ units resolve on four documented grounds: displacement by a free genitive, a reflexive or ἴδιος (2:1, 2:2, 2:3, 2:4, 2:7, 2:9, 2:12, 2:14, 2:16, 2:17, 2:19, 2:20); a determinerless English noun, chiefly God (2:2, 2:4, 2:8, 2:9, 2:10, 2:12, 2:13, 2:14); the nominalizing article of an articular infinitive (2:9, 2:12, 2:16); and rule 31 against rule 90. That last pair is uniform: 2:4, 2:12 and 2:14 have an expressed head noun and empty the article with the relativizer on the participle, while 2:10, 2:13 and 2:15 have none and give the relativizer to the article.

εἰς/πρὸς τό + infinitive is analysed identically at 2:9 ('that'), 2:12 ('to the end that') and 2:16 ('to'): the preposition takes the clause-introducer, the article is unrepresented, and the modal and supplied subject ride with the infinitive. That is rule 24's habit and not three analyses. γίνομαι heads on the lexical word in all six of its units. Rule 106's preverb rides inside its own unit at 2:1, 2:2, 2:15 and 2:16, no expressed preposition competing anywhere in the chapter.

The two rule 37 displacements reconcile token for token: the seven orphaned tokens of 2:7 against the three added units of 2:6, and the six of 2:12 against the three of 2:11. Both directions are recorded on both sides, so neither verse reaches across.

BSB, otherwise. Twenty-two of the twenty-three disagreements are convention differences and expected: thirteen are rule 37 versification tokens in 2:7 and 2:12; five are articles emptied by rules 20, 31, 47 and 61; and μέν (2:18), the first καί of καὶ … καί (2:18) and the sentence-initial ἤ (2:19) are rules 70 and 65 working as written. Only 2:14's καί is an error, and the precedent decided it rather than the score.

Left alone deliberately: 2:20's second article taking the repeated 'our' under rule 76's availability test. Reading it as a discontinuous second realization of ἡμῶν under rule 15 is the competing analysis and the verse note already concedes it; the choice is defensible and touches one verse, so it is a single-verse judgment rather than a chapter split.
